I'm a little worried, to be frank. I watched the whole E3 presentation and wow: they've got a dual-screen app for your smartphone (and a $300 phone case) an iOS base management game, a resource-gathering and building mechanic, and crafting, and they plan to have it all out by November of this year. I wouldn't be surprised if actual radroaches crawled out of people's machines at launch. Bethesda's quality assurance isn't great under the best of circumstances--this is the company that couldn't port Doom to consoles without a few new bugs. I kept thinking throughout their presentation "This is what the dev team was doing instead of focusing on their core product." All I want out of a Fallout game is a wasteland to explore and some mutants to shoot in the groin. I'll withhold my enthusiasm until I learn how much focus the new Rust mechanic took away from the game proper.

--edit- Oh and amiibos because why the hell not.

That's a good point, but that still means that money was diverted from the core game to build all that extra stuff. I'm also concerned because the presenters spent easily a third of the Fallout reveal on these new mechanics. Admittedly there were a lot of them to go through. But it could be that they didn't think wandering around the wastelands and shooting mutants was going to be enough of a draw, and that makes me worried that wandering the wastelands and shooting mutants in Fallout 4 isn't going to be very good. Anyway, all I'm saying at this point is that the E3 presentation failed to sell me on Fallout 4. I'll see what reviewers say when the game comes out. Besides, my general policy with Bethesda is to wait for the GOTY edition--and there's always a GOTY edition. Fewer bugs, and comes packaged with the inevitable DLC.
